# MCP core tools

The tools an agent sees in `tools/list` on `/mcp` (the standard profile; arch §14). Generated from the core tool table, `crates/cutweave-api/mcp_core.toml`, and the command registry.

- **Listed:** 32 tools (28 core and the 4 generic ones), 31489 bytes, about 7873 tokens (`ceil(bytes / 4)`). The budget is 36 tools and 8000 tokens. Every profile's budget is in the table's `[profiles]`, and only there.
- **`/mcp/minimal`** (`--profile minimal`): 10 tools of 12, about 1959 tokens of 3000.
- **`/mcp/full`** (`--profile full`): 32 tools of 36, about 7873 tokens of 8000.
- **`/mcp/described`** (`--profile described`): 32 tools of 36, about 14930 tokens of 16000.
- **Server instructions:** 3413 characters of at most 4096: a map of the command namespaces, how to find, describe and run a command, batches, the revision and undo. Built from the registry and the `[[namespace]]` lines of the core tool table.
- **Loaded at the start:** `project_info`, `timeline_get`, `cutweave_search_commands`, `cutweave_describe_command`, `cutweave_execute` carry `_meta` `"anthropic/alwaysLoad": true`, which asks a client that defers tool definitions (Claude Code's tool search) to load them at the start. They are what an agent needs before it can search; other clients ignore the key. Marked **always** below.
- **Names:** a tool is named after its command with `.` replaced by `_` (`clip.split` is `clip_split`). A core tool is only that command: the same input schema, result and errors as over JSON-RPC and the CLI.
- **Descriptions:** the text below followed by `E.g.` and the example, at most 300 characters. In an example `…` stands for the 32 hex digits of an id.
- **Parameters:** a listed input schema validates exactly like the command's. On `/mcp` it carries no parameter descriptions (they do not fit the budget); `cutweave_describe_command` returns them, with the output schema. `/mcp/described` lists the same tools in the same order with every parameter description, for clients that defer tool definitions and load one when the model asks for it (ADR-0040); the two lists accept the same values.
- **Results:** the command's output as `structuredContent`; the document revision after the call is in the result's `_meta` (`io.cutweave/rev`) and in its first text line. An error is a result with `isError`, a `code`, a `message`, the `path` of the argument when known and a `hint` on what to do next.
- **Revision check:** every tool that is not read-only takes an optional `expected_rev` (the revision a result reported): if the document has moved on, the call fails with `conflict` (`current_rev`, `expected_rev`, and `changed_since`: the items touched in between, or `unknown`) and changes nothing. `/mcp/described` lists the argument on each of those tools; `/mcp`, `/mcp/full` and `/mcp/minimal` accept it without listing it (it does not fit their budget, ADR-0041) and list it on `cutweave_execute`, which reaches every command.

## Core tools

| Tool | Command | Hints | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `audio_set` | `audio.set` | idempotent | Set a clip's fades, volume (dB) or pan; `set.kind` picks which. | `{"item":"itm_…","set":{"kind":"fade","in":"0.5s","out":"1s"}}` |
| `clip_set_speed` | `clip.set_speed` | idempotent | Change a clip's playback speed, 0.1x to 100x; its length changes unless keep is "duration". Linked partners follow. | `{"item":"itm_…","speed":"2x"}` |
| `clip_split` | `clip.split` | - | Split a clip and its linked partners at a timeline time inside it; returns the left and right ids. | `{"item":"itm_…","at":"2.5s"}` |
| `clip_trim` | `clip.trim` | idempotent | Move a clip's start or end edge to a time (`to`) or by an amount (`delta`). Linked partners follow; the main track closes up. | `{"item":"itm_…","edge":"end","delta":"-0.5s"}` |
| `edit_checkpoint` | `edit.checkpoint` | - | Save a restore point of the document before risky edits; cheap. Returns its id. | `{"name":"before-recut"}` |
| `edit_redo` | `edit.redo` | - | Redo your last undone change (`steps` for more). | `{}` |
| `edit_restore` | `edit.restore` | idempotent | Bring the document back to a checkpoint (id or name) as one undoable change; refuses to revert other actors' edits unless force is true. | `{"checkpoint":"before-recut"}` |
| `edit_undo` | `edit.undo` | - | Undo your last change (`steps` for more); other actors' later edits are kept. | `{"steps":2}` |
| `export_start` | `export.start` | destructive | Export a sequence to a video file as a background job; returns job_id for job_wait. Presets: export.list_presets. | `{"path":"C:/out/cut.mp4","preset":"youtube-1080p"}` |
| `item_delete` | `item.delete` | destructive | Delete items and their linked partners; the main track closes up, other tracks keep the gap. | `{"items":["itm_…"]}` |
| `item_move` | `item.move` | - | Move items to a time (`start`) or by `delta`, and/or to another track (`to_track`). Linked partners follow. | `{"item":"itm_…","start":"6s"}` |
| `item_set_props` | `item.set_props` | idempotent | Set some of an item's properties: name, enabled, opacity, audio gain and pan, transform, crop, flip, blend mode. The rest stay. | `{"item":"itm_…","props":{"opacity":0.5,"transform":{"scale":{"x":1.2,"y":1.2}}}}` |
| `job_status` | `job.status` | read-only, idempotent | Get a background job's state, progress and error (media analysis, export). | `{"id":"job_…"}` |
| `job_wait` | `job.wait` | read-only, idempotent | Wait for a background job to finish, at most timeout_ms (max 60000); returns its state. Call again while it is running. | `{"job_id":"job_…","timeout_ms":30000}` |
| `keyframe_set` | `keyframe.set` | idempotent | Animate one property of an item: add or replace keys at sequence times (`at`) or item times (`t`), with an easing to the next key. | `{"item":"itm_…","prop":"opacity","keys":[{"at":"6s","value":0,"easing":"ease_out"},{"at":"8s","value":1}]}` |
| `media_import` | `media.import` | idempotent | Import media files by absolute path. Returns media_ids at once; analysis runs as jobs (job_ids) that job_wait waits for. | `{"paths":["C:/footage/a.mp4"]}` |
| `media_list` | `media.list` | read-only, idempotent | List the project's media with ids, kinds and durations; filter, sort and page. | `{"filter":{"kinds":["video"],"used":false},"limit":20}` |
| `project_info` | `project.info` | read-only, idempotent, **always** | Get the project's name, default format and its sequences with their ids. Start here. | `{}` |
| `project_open` | `project.open` | destructive | Open a project folder or .cutweave file; the current project closes. Fails if that would lose unsaved changes. | `{"path":"C:/projects/trip"}` |
| `render_frame` | `render.frame` | read-only, idempotent | See the frame at a time: returns an image (JPEG, 768 px by default) and the items on screen. Not usable inside cutweave_execute. | `{"t":"2.5s"}` |
| `sequence_create` | `sequence.create` | - | Add a sequence from an aspect preset ("16:9", "9:16", "1:1", ...) or an explicit format; `main_magnetic: true` makes V1 the magnetic main track; returns its id and tracks. | `{"name":"Short","preset":"9:16"}` |
| `sequence_set_format` | `sequence.set_format` | destructive, idempotent | Change a sequence's size, frame rate, sample rate or background; `reframe` says how items adapt to a new size. | `{"sequence":"seq_…","width":1080,"height":1920}` |
| `timeline_add_marker` | `timeline.add_marker` | - | Add a marker at a time of a sequence, or on one of its items (`item`; then `t` is from the item's start). `duration` makes it a range. | `{"sequence":"seq_…","t":"12s","label":"Cut here"}` |
| `timeline_get` | `timeline.get` | read-only, idempotent, **always** | Read a sequence: depth 0 summary, 1 tracks with counts (default), 2 items with ids and times. Page a long one with `range`, `limit` and `cursor`; `detail` "concise" is half the size. | `{"sequence":"seq_…","depth":2,"limit":50}` |
| `timeline_insert` | `timeline.insert` | - | Place a media clip on a track at a time; video with sound also gets a linked audio clip. Returns the new clip ids. | `{"sequence":"seq_…","track":"trk_…","media":"med_…","at":"0s"}` |
| `track_add` | `track.add` | - | Add an empty track to a sequence; returns its id. | `{"sequence":"seq_…","kind":"video"}` |
| `view_get` | `view.get` | idempotent | Read what the user sees in the app: playhead, selection, zoom, active sequence, source in/out marks. | `{}` |
| `view_set` | `view.set` | idempotent | Show the user something in the app: move the playhead, select items, zoom or switch sequence. Changes only the view; not undoable. | `{"patch":{"playhead":"12s","selection":[{"kind":"item","id":"itm_…"}]}}` |

## Generic tools

They reach every command and query that is not hidden, listed or not.

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `cutweave_search_commands` (**always**) | Finds commands and queries by keyword or by the words a user would say (the `[keywords]` of the core tool table) and says how to call each. `detail`: `summary` (default), `names` (names only) or `schema` (adds each hit's input schema, 5 hits at most) |
| `cutweave_describe_command` (**always**) | Returns one command's docs, annotations and full input and output schemas (`name`), or those of up to 8 commands in one call (`names`) |
| `cutweave_execute` (**always**) | Runs one or more commands as one all-or-nothing transaction and one undo step |
| `cutweave_query` | Runs a read-only query by name |
